extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions. The dataset consists of paired top-bottom images with corresponding depth maps, captured from a robot navigating in dynamic human environments using two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor. It includes accurate depth and disparity labels by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images and provides an augmented training set with increased label density through depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbiere, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.citeAs: HELVIPAD: A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a vertical arrangement (19.1 cm baseline) and paired with a synchronized Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor (42.4° vertical field of view, 10 fps) mounted 45.0 cm below the bottom camera. The rig was mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis and navigated through indoor (e.g., corridors, halls) and outdoor (e.g., squares, parking, footpaths) settings on a university campus under diverse lighting conditions (day, night) and weather (cloudy, sunny). A central processor managed data capture and ensured device synchronization. 29 video sequences were collected between December 2023 and February 2024 at 10 Hz frame rate.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of equirectangular images from two 360° cameras (Ricoh Theta V, 3840×1920 pixels at 30 fps) and LiDAR point clouds (Ouster OS1-64, 64 beams, 10 fps). Depth labels were obtained by projecting 3D LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images, with an average pixel error of 8.0 pixels (0.40% of image diagonal) after calibration.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A depth completion pipeline was applied to increase label density from 12% to 61% by temporally aggregating point clouds (4 previous and 4 succeeding frames), interpolating depth on spherical grid points using k-nearest neighbors (k=17), and filtering points based on uncertainty and out-of-distribution thresholds. The pipeline increased the ratio of labeled pixels from 12% to 61% while maintaining low error rates.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were cropped to remove unnecessary regions (sky, ground) and downsized from 1024 to 512 pixels width for efficient training. Depth maps were converted to disparity maps using spherical disparity equations. Photometric data augmentation was applied during training to handle lighting variability.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent cropping to remove sky and ground regions, downsizing from 1024×512 to 1920×512 pixels resolution, and synchronization between LiDAR and camera frames using hardware-triggered flash synchronization. LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images with calibration accuracy of 8.0 pixels average error. Depth completion was applied to increase label density from sparse LiDAR measurements.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Depth and disparity labels were created by projecting 3D LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images, with depth completion applied to increase label density. The dataset includes 39,553 paired images with corresponding depth and disparity maps after preprocessing.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Depth completion pipeline using k-nearest neighbors interpolation (k=17) and spherical grid projection; LiDAR-to-image mapping optimization using BFGS algorithm for rotation/translation alignment
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is maintained by the VITA lab at EPFL with versioning information available through the project website. The dataset includes train-val and test splits with no scene overlap between splits. The authors plan to update the dataset with additional sequences and annotations as needed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables development of depth estimation models for mobile robots in real-world applications such as autonomous driving, healthcare, and agriculture where accurate 3D representations of dynamic human environments are crucial for navigation and interaction. The dataset's focus on omnidirectional imaging addresses limitations of conventional stereo systems in capturing comprehensive spatial awareness.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may exhibit biases toward university campus environments, with sequences collected primarily in indoor corridors, halls, outdoor squares, parking areas, and footpaths. The dataset includes diverse lighting conditions (day, night) and weather (cloudy, sunny), but may not fully represent all possible real-world scenarios. Indoor sequences show more rapid decline in pixel percentage beyond 10 meters compared to outdoor scenes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limited representation of fast-moving objects (e.g., cars) due to temporal aggregation constraints in depth completion. LiDAR point clouds are sparse, especially for objects at far range, which affects depth label density. The dataset focuses on university campus environments and may not generalize to all real-world scenarios. Depth completion may not provide labels at object boundaries where precise boundary locations are ambiguous.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models. The dataset serves as a foundational resource for developing and benchmarking models capable of navigating in human environments, with applications in autonomous systems, robotics, and computer vision research.
